parts.contentJson: {"text":"\"Design a modern, friendly, and clean web application interface for an educational financial & ethical consumption tool named 'TrueCost'. Target audience: High school students (Gen Z). Color palette: Emerald Green (#10B981) as primary, Warm Amber (#F59E0B) for alert/impact metrics, Off-White/Light Mint (#F0FDF4) for backgrounds, and Charcoal (#1F2937) for text. Modern rounded typography (Inter or Plus Jakarta Sans). Includes 2 main features: 1) Interactive TrueCost Calculator for snack purchases, and 2) Snack Life Cycle Literacy Education Hub. Make it engaging, gamified, and easy to understand. Make this adaptable to every interface type, from desktop, tablets, and phones.\"","providerOptions":{}}
{"text":"I’ll inspect the existing app and its design patterns, then implement a focused responsive TrueCost experience across desktop, tablet, and mobile.","textMode":"visible_message"}

{"toolCallId":"ea749375-c58f-8778-82c9-6053a652326d","toolName":"figaro.plugin/skill","resultJson":"{\"success\":true,\"content\":\"# Goal\\nUse the design system (DS) as the primary source of truth for how the product should look and behave. When the DS doesn't cover a requirement, make the smallest extension consistent with its design intent.\\n\\n# Things to avoid\\n\\n- Do not guess package names, exports, props, etc. Make sure you are using actual APIs.\\n- Do not replace an available component / token with another generic component library the project doesn't use.\\n- Do not modify files inside the DS module.\\n- Do not write raw HTML elements like `<button`, `<input`, `<select`, `<textarea`, `<a>`, `<h1>/<h2>/etc.`.\\n  — Do not use manual / raw tokens -- hex colors, `px`/`rem` literals in class names or inline styles, and `style={{ color`/`fontSize`/`fontWeight`/`padding`/`margin`. Use DS tokens instead.\\n\\n# Priorities\\n\\nWhen sources disagree, follow the highest priority source in this order:\\n\\n1. User instructions, especially any requested exceptions\\n2. DS components, icons, tokens, styles, and guidance\\n3. Screenshots or Figma designs' opinions about styling — only when the DS has no opinion\\n4. Implementation examples in codebase\\n5. Note the packages they import from.\\n\\nInfer what DS setup the project should use, making note of decisions like what modules should be responsible for:\\n\\n- Components\\n- Design tokens\\n- Colors, typography, spacing\\n\\n## Discovering the DS\\n\\nDo not guess package names, exports, or props. Verify the APIs you intend to use with the smallest amount of inspection needed.\\n\\n  1. Identify the designated DS and read its `package.json`. Check the version, exports, types, and stylesheet entry points to establish supported imports. Read its setup instructions alongside it.\\n  2. Prefer a consolidated component catalog for discovery, such as a .json or a summary .md file. Search or extract relevant entries from large catalogs. Map the UI elements needed for the brief to available components, including typography, surfaces, and interactive controls.\\n  3. Read component-specific documentation and examples only for selected components, when the catalog does not explain the needed usage patterns, composition, variants, or accessibility guidance.\\n  4. Read typings such as .d.ts files for unresolved API questions. Check required props, allowed values, hook return shapes, or import declarations when documentation omits details or typechecking fails.\\n  5. Diverge incrementally from the DS only when you can't find a requirement: Existing component with the right variant → composition of DS primitives → a local component built from DS tokens → raw values (almost never).\\n\\nMatch semantic, not appearance. {"text":"**Evaluating portal redesign**

I need to redesign the current tabs into card format for the portal. It could be simplified with a header logo and hero title/subtitle, along with two cards. I'm thinking about making them interactive with click toggles or redirects, but we don’t currently have routes. Maybe the cards could scroll, and maintaining status to display a toast is a thought. Using buttons with click interactions to update `selectedPortal` seems better, but I’m cautious about URL hash manipulation since it might not be ideal. I want to keep it user-friendly.

**Planning app updates**

I’m thinking about using my design skills to update the app and adjust the CSS. The header should feature only a profile icon, not a badge. I want to center the hero section and include two cards, using icons for a calculator and a book, and possibly making the cards clickable as a whole. 

I’m considering how to handle interactivity for navigation. Maybe I can use the `openPortal` function that sets the status text without a real destination. Since users expect a redirect and there are no pages, I could use `location.hash` to render the portal. I want to preserve the AppButton while implementing these changes!

{"toolCallId":"33503f1d-066e-833c-a199-5f476843d429","toolName":"figaro.plugin/skill","resultJson":"{\"success\":true,\"content\":\"# Payload App Auth\\n\\nUse this skill for auth in the generated website/app, not for Make file access\\nor Payload Admin login.\\n\\nKeep three auth systems separate:\\n\\n- Figma/Make access controls who can view or edit the Make file.\\n- Payload Admin auth controls who can manage CMS/admin content.\\n- Generated app auth controls who can log into the published app.\\n\\nDo not use generated app auth to grant Payload Admin access, and do not use\\nPayload Admin users for public app signup. Payload Admin auth is\\nplatform/control-plane behavior and may use Figma SSO and/or Payload-native auth\\nsuch as username/password or third-party SSO. Do not build or modify Payload\\nAdmin login unless the user explicitly asks for CMS/admin access behavior.\\nTreat package-level CLI OAuth and Payload Admin OAuth behavior as\\nplatform-owned; do not reimplement it in app auth.\\n\\nIf the user is asking who can access `/admin`, manage CMS content, or sign in as\\na CMS editor, do not solve that by installing `payload-auth` or adding generated\\napp login. Work with the existing Payload Admin / `@payloadcms/figma` /\\nplatform-owned admin auth setup and add only the requested admin roles or access\\nrules.\\n\\n## Decide The Auth Shape\\n\\n- If the user asks for app login/accounts and does not specify a method, ask\\n  once whether they want Payload email/password or OAuth/social login. If the\\n  runtime requires proceeding without a choice, use Payload-native\\n  email/password because it does not require third-party secrets.\\n- If the user asks for email/password or username/password, use a Payload\\n  auth-enabled app-user collection and Payload auth operations.\\n- If the user asks for Google OAuth, magic links, Apple, GitHub, Microsoft, or a\\n  custom provider, implement the requested provider as generated app auth. Use\\n  Payload for the app-user records and prefer the public `payload-auth`\\n  framework when it is compatible with the project. Do not wire the provider\\n  into Payload Admin Panel auth.\\n- If the user explicitly asks for Supabase auth, use the Supabase flow instead\\n  of Payload.\\n\\nUse Payload for durable app-user records whenever app data needs to be tied to a\\nsigned-in person. For OAuth, magic links, email delivery, and other\\nsecret-backed work, use existing supported auth/email libraries or framework\\nintegrations in server-only code. Do not hand-roll provider protocols, token\\nvalidation, cookie/session security, or email verification flows.\\n\\nIf adding auth changes ownership, privacy, or relationships for existing domain\\nrecords, use `payload-data-modeling` before changing the schema or data.\\n\\n## App User Collections\\n\\nKeep Payload Admin/CMS users and app end users in separate auth collections. Do\\nnot choose the app auth collection by name alone.\\n\\nBefore implementing app auth:\\n\\n1. Inspect `src/payload.config.ts` and identify the collection configured as\\n   `admin.user`. That collection is the admin/CMS user collection.\\n2. If `data-users` exists, treat it as the likely Figma-managed admin/CMS\\n   collection, but still verify `admin.user`. Do not assume `users` is available\\n   for app-level end users unless `admin.user` points somewhere else.\\n3. If `users` is configured as `admin.user`, do not reuse it for public app\\n   accounts. Create a separate app auth collection such as `Customers`,\\n   `Members`, or `Patients`. Never use the admin/CMS collection for public\\n   signup or with `createAppAuth`.\\n\\nDo not put public app accounts in the admin/CMS user collection, and do not give\\napp users CMS/admin capabilities. Use an existing app-user auth collection only\\nwhen it is already separate from the admin/CMS collection.\\n\\nFor new email/password apps with a separate CMS collection such as `admins`,\\ndefault to `Users` / `users`, or use a domain collection name that matches the\\nproduct. Preserve a compatible existing app collection and its accounts.\\n\\nFor an auth-enabled domain collection:\\n\\n- Set `auth: true` for email/password users. For OAuth-only users, set\\n  `auth: { disableLocalStrategy: true }` and key the record on the provider's\\n  stable id: with the local strategy on, `payload.create` without a password\\n  throws a `password` `ValidationError`, and\\n  `enableFields` adds a required, unique `email`, which providers can omit\\n  (Spotify's February 2026 Development Mode changes remove it). Keep email\\n  optional and never refuse a sign-in for lacking it:\\n\\n  ```ts\\n  auth: { disableLocalStrategy: true }, // no Payload password or email fields\\n  fields: [\\n    { name: 'providerId', type: 'text', required: true, unique: true, index: true }, // Google sub, Spotify id\\n    { name: 'email', type: 'email' }, // optional; absent for some providers\\n  ],\\n  ```\\n- Include the user-facing profile fields the app needs, such as name, avatar,\\n  role, status, onboarding fields, or relationships to domain records.\\n- Add access rules so users can read/update their own profile and protected\\n  records, while public pages only read public data.\\n- Prevent app users from accessing Payload Admin. Do not configure a public\\n  app-user collection as `admin.user`. Use `admin.hidden` only to keep\\n  non-admin app-user collections out of the admin sidebar; it is not a login\\n  gate by itself.\\n- Register the collection in `src/payload.config.ts`. Payload regenerates\\n  `src/payload-types.ts` automatically; do not manually regenerate types.\\n\\nDo not create custom password hashing, custom session storage, or a parallel\\nauth database from scratch.\\n\\nApp users and CMS admins are separate identities with independent sessions. Do\\nnot link or reuse records between the two auth collections. Internal tools that\\nrequire CMS-admin auth must continue using the existing CMS auth flow instead\\nof `createAppAuth`.\\n\\n## Email/Password\\n\\nFor email/password auth, create or reuse a server-only `src/lib/app-auth.ts`\\nmodule that exports a `createAppAuth` factory. Configure it with the app-user\\ncollection slug, for example `createAppAuth('users')`. The factory owns app\\nlogin, logout, refresh, and current-user resolution through a dedicated\\nHTTP-only `app-session` cookie independently of CMS auth.\\n\\nThe factory must read only `app-session`, validate only that token against the\\nconfigured app-user collection, and reject identities from other collections.\\nConstruct a new `Headers` object containing only that token as JWT authorization,\\nthen pass those isolated headers to `payload.auth`. Check `user.collection`, not\\na top-level `collection` property on the auth result:\\n\\n```ts\\nconst token = (await cookies()).get('app-session')?.value\\nif (!token) return null\\n\\nconst authHeaders = new Headers({ Authorization: `JWT ${token}` })\\nconst { user } = await payload.auth({ headers: authHeaders })\\nif (!user || user.collection !== appUserCollection) return null\\n```\\n\\nNever pass `await headers()`, an incoming request `Headers` object, or its\\n`cookie` header to app-user authentication. Those ambient headers can contain\\nboth the CMS-admin cookie and the app cookie. The CMS strategy may win first,\\ncausing a valid app login to resolve as the CMS identity and then appear signed\\nout. Reuse the existing Payload loader and bootstrap; do not change package\\nversions for this auth isolation.\\n\\nBuild the minimum complete flow:\\n\\n- Create-account UI with email plus password.\\n- Login UI with email plus password.\\n- Logout.\\n- A server-side current-user helper using the configured `createAppAuth` instance.\\n- Protected pages/actions redirect or return a clear signed-out state.\\n- User-owned data queries filter by the authenticated user.\\n\\nIf the user asks for username/password, still collect email for Payload login\\nunless you explicitly implement and test username-based auth support. When\\nrepairing an existing app whose app-user collection already supports username\\nauth, preserve its username-only login UI and confirm username login works;\\ndo not replace it with email.\\n\\nWhen reading or writing app-user-owned data with Payload's local API, pass the\\nisolated app user and set `overrideAccess: false`. CMS\\nlogout must not affect the `app-session` cookie. The two sessions are\\nindependent: a user may be signed into both concurrently.\\n\\nDo not include email confirmation, password reset, magic links, or transactional\\nemail by default. Those require a third-party email provider. If the user asks\\nfor them, use the environment-variable card flow for provider secrets and build\\nthe email work server-side.\\n\\n## OAuth And Social Login\\n\\nFor Google OAuth or any social/OIDC provider, prefer the public `payload-auth`\\nframework when it is compatible with the project. It integrates Payload with\\nBetter Auth and exposes Payload plugin entry points such as\\n`payload-auth/better-auth/plugin`. Use the package's current docs and installed\\ntypes for the exact API. Do not hand-roll Google/OAuth as the default\\nimplementation path.\\n\\nDo not use `@payloadcms/figma` CLI OAuth, Figma/Payload control-plane OAuth, or\\nPayload Admin OAuth as generated app auth. Those are for Figma/package login or\\nCMS/admin access, not public app login.\\n\\nIf `payload-auth` cannot be used because of version compatibility, missing\\nprovider support, or unclear setup, pause when possible and ask before choosing\\nanother framework. If the user explicitly requires OAuth and implementation must\\nproceed, use a mature server-side auth/OIDC framework. Keep callbacks, state\\nvalidation, code exchange, identity verification, session issuance, and refresh\\nbehavior in that supported framework rather than recreating the protocol.\\n\\nFor OAuth in a Payload-backed app:\\n\\n- Use the environment-variable card flow for client IDs, client secrets, and\\n  other provider secrets; never ask for secrets in chat. Put the framework's\\n  session secret on the same card (`AUTH_SECRET` for Auth.js/NextAuth,\\n  `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` for Better Auth); a published site without it fails at\\n  sign-in. For Auth.js, name the provider's variables `AUTH_<PROVIDER>_ID` and\\n  `AUTH_<PROVIDER>_SECRET`, such as `AUTH_GOOGLE_ID`, and read those names in\\n  the preview routes too: a bare `Google()` reads only them, and under any other\\n  name published sign-in sends `client_id=undefined`.\\n- Surface redirect/callback URLs the user must paste into the provider console\\n  as chat instructions, never in the secret card. See\\n  [Redirect And Callback URLs](#redirect-and-callback-urls) for when to say it\\n  and what it must say.\\n- Map the provider identity to a Payload app-user record when the app needs user\\n  data, ownership, roles, preferences, bookings, subscriptions, or profiles.\\n- On first successful sign-in, find or create the Payload app-user record by the\\n  stable provider id (Google `sub`, Spotify `id`), and reuse it later. This sync\\n  runs before any app user exists, and Payload 4's Local API defaults to\\n  `overrideAccess: false`, so under app-user access rules it throws `Forbidden`\\n  (\\\"You are not allowed to perform this action.\\\") on every sign-in. Pass\\n  `overrideAccess: true` on its find, create and update calls, in server-only\\n  sign-in code and nowhere else:\\n\\n  ```ts\\n  // The identity sync runs before any app user exists, so it bypasses access here only.\\n  const { docs } = await payload.find({ collection: 'users', where: { providerId: { equals: id } }, limit: 1, overrideAccess: true })\\n  ```\\n- The final app must have one server-side current-user helper that resolves the\\n  active session to a Payload app-user record. Protected pages, server actions,\\n  route handlers, and user-owned data queries must all use that helper unless\\n  the provider session is bridged into Payload-native auth.\\n- Store provider identifiers and non-secret profile metadata needed for account\\n  linking. {"toolCallId":"d7145b71-5f4d-8d82-83ae-16a0c9851b72","toolName":"figaro.plugin/skill","resultJson":"{\"success\":true,\"content\":\"# Payload Data Modeling\\n\\nUse this skill before editing Payload schema or changing how app data is\\nrepresented. This skill decides the model and migration plan. Use\\n`payload-content` afterward to read, seed, or mutate real Payload documents\\nthrough the project-installed Payload CLI.\\n\\nFor editor-managed images, galleries, portfolios, file uploads, or public/private\\ndownloads, load `payload-framework` before implementing media storage, image\\nrendering, or cache headers. This skill owns the schema; `payload-framework`\\nowns the media delivery rules.\\n\\nFor editor-managed SEO metadata, administrator-defined forms, or durable\\nbackground work, load `payload-framework` before choosing plugins or jobs.\\n\\n## Model The Domain\\n\\n- Model durable app concepts as first-class collections or globals, not generic\\n  `items` or static arrays.\\n- Let domain behavior drive the schema. Ask what users create, edit, reuse,\\n  search, publish, own, permission, archive, and report on.\\n- Prefer relationships when a concept has its own lifecycle, admin workflow,\\n  permissions, public page, reporting needs, or appears in many places.\\n- Keep simple primitive fields when the value is truly local to one document and\\n  will not be filtered, reused, owned, edited, permissioned, or linked elsewhere.\\n- Avoid turning every noun into a collection. Use the simplest model that keeps\\n  the source of truth clear and supports the requested workflows.\\n- Use uploads related to `media` for CMS-managed images and files.\\n- Use unique slugs for public detail pages when users need stable URLs. Route\\n  files should use the shared `findBySlug()` helper from `src/lib/payload.ts`\\n  instead of duplicating the query inline. When the routing field changes\\n  (e.g. from `slug` to `title` or `handle`), update all route files to use\\n  `findByField()` with the new field name.\\n- When an editor-managed collection backs public list and slug-detail routes,\\n  plan cached list/detail reads plus `afterChange`/`afterDelete` invalidation\\n  hooks with the schema. Invalidate the list and the old and new detail keys on\\n  create, update, publish/unpublish, delete, and slug change; a `revalidate`\\n  interval is not a substitute. Do not infer an editorial\\n  workflow merely because a record lives in Payload.\\n- Organize the admin sidebar around user workflows. Do not bolt them on after the UI works.\\n\\n- Public content may be readable by anyone.\\n- Private, user-submitted, staff-only, operational, booking, order, message, and\\n  contact records need explicit `access` rules.\\n- User-owned records need an owner relationship and access filters scoped to the\\n  authenticated app user.\\n- Set owner relationships server-side from the current user. For data-shaping or destructive changes, make a short data transition plan\\n   and confirm it with the user before editing source code or mutating\\n   documents (see \\\"Confirm Before Destructive Or Data-Shaping Changes\\\").\\n   Non-destructive additive changes proceed without confirmation.\\n\\nTreat follow-up requests after an app/schema has been created as existing-app\\nedits, even in the same chat. Make code history and Payload document data are\\nseparate; rolling back code does not roll back Payload data.\\n\\n## Confirm Before Destructive Or Data-Shaping Changes\\n\\nAfter inspecting the schema and documents, decide whether the change is\\nadditive-only or potentially destructive.\\n\\nNon-destructive additive changes proceed **without** confirmation:\\n\\n- Adding a new collection, global, optional field, or optional relationship.\\n- Widening a constraint, relaxing validation, or adding admin-only presentation.\\n\\nPotentially destructive or data-shaping changes **require** confirmation:\\n\\n- Deleting a collection, global, or field that holds data.\\n- Narrowing or changing a field's type, or tightening constraints (`required`,\\n  `unique`, enum narrowing, min/max/format validation), in a way that can lose\\n  or invalidate existing values.\\n- Renaming a collection or field without a migration that preserves values (a\\n  destructive rename).\\n- Changing a relationship — cardinality, target collection, or direction — in a\\n  way that can orphan or invalidate existing references.\\n- Any document mutation that deletes, overwrites, or bulk-edits existing data as\\n  part of the change.\\n\\nBefore any potentially destructive schema edit or document mutation, always call\\n`mcp__plugin_conversation_ask_user_question__ask_user_question` and wait for the\\nuser's response. {"toolCallId":"5688af83-dfe3-8c42-9474-5cb0caa5eceb","toolName":"figaro.plugin/skill","resultJson":"{\"success\":true,\"content\":\"---\\ntitle: Server and Client Components\\ndescription: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client.\\nrelated:\\n title: Next Steps\\n description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned in this page.\\n links:\\n - app/api-reference/directives/use-client\\n---\\n\\nBy default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.\\n\\nThis page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.\\n\\n## When to use Server and Client Components?\\n\\nThe client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case.\\n\\nUse **Client Components** when you need:\\n\\n- [State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) and [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events). E.g. `onClick`, `onChange`.\\n- [Lifecycle logic](https://react.dev/learn/lifecycle-of-reactive-effects). E.g. `useEffect`.\\n- Browser-only APIs. E.g. `localStorage`, `window`, `Navigator.geolocation`, etc.\\n- [Custom hooks](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks).\\n\\nUse **Server Components** when you need:\\n\\n- Fetch data from databases or APIs close to the source.\\n- Use API keys, tokens, and other secrets without exposing them to the client.\\n- Reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser.\\n- Improve the [First Contentful Paint (FCP)](https://web.dev/fcp/), and stream content progressively to the client.\\n\\nFor example, the `` component is a Server Component that fetches data about a post, and passes it as props to the `` which handles client-side interactivity.\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/[id]/page.tsx\\\" highlight={1,17} switcher\\nimport LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'\\nimport { getPost } from '@/lib/data'\\n\\nexport default async function Page({\\n params,\\n}: {\\n params: Promise<{ id: string }>\\n}) {\\n const { id } = await params\\n const post = await getPost(id)\\n\\n return (\\n
\\n

{post.title}

\\n {/* ... */}\\n \\n

\\n )\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/[id]/page.js\\\" highlight={1,12} switcher\\nimport LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'\\nimport { getPost } from '@/lib/data'\\n\\nexport default async function Page({ params }) {\\n const post = await getPost(params.id)\\n\\n return (\\n

The rendering work is split into chunks, by individual route segments ([layouts and pages](/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages)):\\n\\n- **Server Components** are rendered into a special data format called the React Server Component Payload (RSC Payload).\\n- **Client Components** and the RSC Payload are used to [prerender](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) HTML.\\n\\n> **What is the React Server Component Payload (RSC)?**\\n>\\n> The RSC Payload is a compact binary representation of the rendered React Server Components tree. It's used by React on the client to update the browser's DOM. The RSC Payload contains:\\n>\\n> - The rendered result of Server Components\\n> - Placeholders for where Client Components should be rendered and references to their JavaScript files\\n> - Any props passed from a Server Component to a Client Component\\n\\n### On the client (first load)\\n\\nThen, on the client:\\n\\n1. **HTML** is used to immediately show a fast non-interactive preview of the route to the user.\\n2. **RSC Payload** is used to reconcile the Client and Server Component trees.\\n3. **JavaScript** is used to hydrate Client Components and make the application interactive.\\n\\n> **What is hydration?**\\n>\\n> Hydration is React's process for attaching [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events) to the DOM, to make the static HTML interactive.\\n\\n### Subsequent Navigations\\n\\nOn subsequent navigations:\\n\\n- The **RSC Payload** is prefetched and cached for instant navigation.\\n- **Client Components** are rendered entirely on the client, without the server-rendered HTML.\\n\\n## Examples\\n\\n### Using Client Components\\n\\nYou can create a Client Component by adding the [`\\\"use client\\\"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use-client) directive at the top of the file, above your imports.\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/ui/counter.tsx\\\" highlight={1} switcher\\n'use client'\\n\\nimport { useState } from 'react'\\n\\nexport default function Counter() {\\n const [count, setCount] = useState(0)\\n\\n return (\\n

{"toolCallId":"1ee18e2a-c752-89d1-9a45-0ec8df9625db","toolName":"figaro.plugin/skill","resultJson":"{\"success\":true,\"content\":\"# Preview OAuth implementation\\n\\nThe preview iframe and its top-level popup have different cookie partitions. Use the popup for provider consent and the iframe for installing the app session. Providers can sever `window.opener` during navigation; use it only for the initial same-origin handshake.\\n\\nCopy [preview-oauth-browser.ts](preview-oauth-browser.ts) and [preview-oauth-server.ts](preview-oauth-server.ts) into the app's client/server library directories respectively. Keep their source/origin checks and atomic transaction transitions. The helpers are executable, tested reference code; adapt imports and the Payload session adapter, not the security protocol.\\n\\n## Client and popup\\n\\nThe iframe calls `openPreviewOAuth()` directly from its click handler. It opens the fixed `/api/auth/preview-signin` path with `_blank` synchronously, verifies the popup's first message by exact origin and window identity, and acknowledges its random secret. It resolves only after a second verified message confirms that the server created the transaction, so polling cannot race the start POST. Keep the connect deadline and the wait for that confirmation on separate timers: a first compile can push the start POST past the handshake budget, and one timer covering both abandons a sign-in that is still running. The connect deadline is 45 seconds because the bridge page's own first compile on a fresh dev server takes several seconds; do not shorten it. A disabled preview gate rejects before navigation, and a failed start POST rejects as soon as the bridge reports it; offer email/password or the published site. The iframe bundle exposes availability as `window.__figmaPreviewOAuthPopupsAllowed === true` and dispatches `figma:preview-oauth-availability` on `document` when it changes. Read availability in click handlers or after mount; branching server-rendered markup on it would cause a hydration mismatch.\\n\\nThen wait with `waitForPreviewOAuthSession()`, which polls `POST /api/auth/preview-exchange` until the popup finishes or the five-minute transaction expires. Give it a fresh `AbortController` per sign-in and abort that controller on unmount, as below. Do not guard the wait with a mounted ref: in development, Strict Mode runs every effect cleanup once on mount, which leaves such a flag false so the wait never polls.\\n\\n```tsx\\nconst router = useRouter()\\nconst pendingSignIn = useRef<AbortController | null>(null)\\n// Aborts only a sign-in in progress, so Strict Mode's extra cleanup is harmless.\\nuseEffect(() => () => pendingSignIn.current?.abort(), [])\\n\\nasync function onClick() {\\n  pendingSignIn.current?.abort()\\n  const controller = (pendingSignIn.current = new AbortController())\\n  try {\\n    const secret = await openPreviewOAuth() // window.open happens before this await\\n    const outcome = await waitForPreviewOAuthSession(secret, controller.signal)\\n    // From app-session-browser.ts: updates components reading `authSession`, then router.refresh().\\n    if (outcome === 'complete') await announceSessionChange(router)\\n    // expired: offer a new sign-in; aborted: it unmounted, do nothing.\\n  } catch {\\n    // Blocked, not connected or unavailable: show a message and offer a retry. Uncaught, a\\n    // rejection inside startTransition replaces the page with its error boundary.\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nDo not put the secret in a URL, fragment, local storage or OAuth state. Do not accept a caller-provided `h` or provide a direct-link fallback. Randomness alone does not prevent an attacker from choosing a handle and sending another browser its signin URL.\\n\\n`GET /api/auth/preview-signin` serves only the bridge page. Reject query parameters. Generate a random bootstrap CSRF secret server-side, set it in a `__Host-pv_bootstrap` cookie (`HttpOnly; Secure; Path=/; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=300`), and supply the same secret to the bridge's client component. Set `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on every preview auth response. Never log cookies, query parameters or request bodies on these routes. Do log the caught error's message where `preview-complete` calls `store.fail`: it is the only record of why a sign-in ended in 410, and it shows up in `figma logs tail .figma/make/dev --stream stderr`.\\n\\nA page cannot set cookies, so make this path a route handler that sets the cookie and redirects to the bridge page at its own path. That page reads the cookie server-side and passes the secret to the client component. Redirect with a path. Next builds `request.url` and `request.nextUrl` from the server's bind address, `0.0.0.0:3000`, so `new URL('/bridge', request.url)` sends the popup to `0.0.0.0` and it shows \\\"refused to connect\\\". `NextResponse.redirect` rejects a bare path, so return a plain `Response`:\\n\\n```ts\\nexport function GET(request: Request) {\\n  const headers = new Headers({ 'cache-control': 'no-store', 'referrer-policy': 'no-referrer' })\\n  if (new URL(request.url).search) return new Response(null, { status: 400, headers })\\n  headers.append('set-cookie', `__Host-pv_bootstrap=${newPreviewOAuthSecret()}; HttpOnly; Secure; Path=/; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=300`)\\n  headers.set('location', '/api/auth/preview-signin/bridge') // a path, never new URL(path, request.url)\\n  return new Response(null, { status: 303, headers })\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThe bridge calls:\\n\\n```ts\\nawait startPreviewOAuthBridge(async (secret) => {\\n  const response = await fetch('/api/auth/preview-start', {\\n    method: 'POST',\\n    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\\n    body: JSON.stringify({ secret, csrf: bootstrapCsrf }),\\n  })\\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Preview sign-in unavailable')\\n  return (await response.json()).authorizationUrl\\n})\\n```\\n\\nIf there is no opener, its origin/window is wrong, or the handshake times out, stop. Do not recover using a URL handle. Verify in the actual preview that the opener survives the initial bridge navigation. Once the provider opens, do not use `popup.closed` to stop polling: COOP can make it report closed while consent is still running.\\n\\n## Server routes\\n\\nPut the bridge and callback pages inside the route group that holds the site's root layout, for example `src/app/(frontend)/api/auth/preview-signin/bridge/page.tsx` and `src/app/(frontend)/api/auth/preview-callback/page.tsx`. Their URLs are unchanged. A page outside every root layout renders without `<html>` and `<body>`, and in the preview Next covers the popup with a \\\"Missing <html> and <body> tags\\\" error.\\n\\nUse one `createPreviewOAuthStore<JWT>()` instance (`JWT` from `next-auth/jwt`) shared across route modules and HMR, for example on `globalThis`. It expires transactions after five minutes and consumes callbacks and sessions once. This in-memory implementation is appropriate for a single-process preview; multiple processes require equivalent atomic operations in a shared store. Losing the store on restart requires a new sign-in, never reconstructing a session from callback input.\\n\\nThe trusted origin for the POST checks is the configured browser-facing sandbox origin (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` in the Payload template), not `Origin`, `Host`, or `x-forwarded-proto` from the request. The envelope lasts two hours from minting and identifies a durable routing key, not a particular container. The app's five-minute transaction deadline is separate.\\n3. Set `__Host-pv_handle` to that secret and `__Host-pv_nonce` to the returned nonce, both `HttpOnly; Secure; Path=/; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=300` in the popup's cookie jar.\\n4. Send `state = [statePrefix, nonce, Buffer.from('/api/auth/preview-callback').toString('base64url')].join('.')`. The prefix itself has three segments, so the nonce is at index **3** and the callback path at index **4**.\\n5. Compute the S256 challenge from the returned PKCE verifier. Build the provider authorization URL with this state, challenge, client ID and the exact injected redirect URI. Return it as JSON. A 302 from this fetch endpoint would fetch the provider instead of navigating the popup.\\n\\n**GET `/api/auth/preview-callback`:**\\n\\nServes only the callback page, with the same `no-store` and `no-referrer` headers. Reject query parameters. Figma's callback host forwards the provider's parameters in the URL fragment, which never reaches a server or a request log; the page hands them to the POST below. Call the helper from an effect with no guard of your own: a second call on the same page, which Strict Mode makes in development, returns the first call's result.\\n\\n```ts\\nawait completePreviewOAuthCallback(async (callback) => {\\n  const response = await fetch('/api/auth/preview-complete', {\\n    method: 'POST',\\n    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\\n    body: JSON.stringify({ callback }),\\n  })\\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Preview sign-in failed')\\n})\\n```\\n\\n**POST `/api/auth/preview-complete`:**\\n\\nRequire `isPreviewOAuthPost(request, trustedOrigin)`, then `const params = readPreviewOAuthCallback(await request.json())`; reject null. Read `state`, `code` and `error` from `params`, never from the request URL. Read the handle and nonce from the popup's cookies. Call `store.takeCallback(handle, state.split('.')[3], popupNonceCookie)` before reading `code` or `error`; reject null. This check binds a provider callback to the same browser that started it. A provider URL opened in another browser must fail even if its server-side state entry exists. Clear the flow cookies on terminal responses. Exchange the code using the returned verifier and exactly the same injected `redirect_uri` used for authorization. Validate the provider identity, find/create the Payload app user, and call `store.complete(handle, claims)` once with the claims the app's Auth.js `jwt` callback returns for that user. If the provider returned `error`, or the exchange, identity check or app-user lookup fails, call `store.fail(handle)` so the iframe's next poll gets 410 instead of 202 until expiry. Once the POST settles, the page closes the popup or shows completion; neither the page nor this route installs the app session cookie.\\n\\n**POST `/api/auth/preview-exchange`:**\\n\\nRequire `isPreviewOAuthPost(request, trustedOrigin)`, then validate the JSON secret and call `store.consume(secret)`. Return 202 for pending, 410 for missing, expired or failed, or 204 with the app session cookie for complete. Only this iframe request installs the cookie, and Auth.js must read it back. It writes the whole token as one cookie, and browsers silently drop a cookie over 4 KB, which leaves the user signed out with no error. Auth.js splits its own large cookies, so only the preview breaks. Keep the claims to identity and provider tokens, and fetch provider data such as playlists or top tracks on the server for each request. Take the cookie's name, attributes and lifetime from one module, and encode the token with that name as its `salt` and that lifetime as its `maxAge`: Auth.js derives the session key from the cookie name, so a different name or salt leaves the user signed out. Configure Auth.js with `session: { strategy: 'jwt', maxAge: SESSION_MAX_AGE }`, and give it no `adapter` and no custom `jwt.encode`/`decode`. An adapter switches Auth.js to database sessions, which never read this cookie, and a custom codec cannot read what `encode` wrote.\\n\\n```ts\\n// src/lib/session-cookie.ts\\nexport const SESSION_COOKIE = '__Host-authjs.session-token'\\nexport const CSRF_COOKIE = '__Host-authjs.csrf-token'\\n// Seconds; Auth.js's default. Change it only here.\\nexport const SESSION_MAX_AGE = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60\\nexport const SESSION_COOKIE_OPTIONS = {\\n  httpOnly: true,\\n  secure: true,\\n  sameSite: 'none',\\n  path: '/',\\n  partitioned: true,\\n} as const\\n\\n// src/auth.ts, below the AUTH_URL pin\\nexport const { handlers, auth, signIn, signOut } = NextAuth({\\n  trustHost: true,\\n  providers: [Google],\\n  session: { strategy: 'jwt', maxAge: SESSION_MAX_AGE },\\n  cookies: {\\n    sessionToken: { name: SESSION_COOKIE, options: SESSION_COOKIE_OPTIONS },\\n    csrfToken: { name: CSRF_COOKIE, options: SESSION_COOKIE_OPTIONS },\\n  },\\n})\\n\\n// src/app/api/auth/preview-exchange/route.ts, once store.consume returned { status: 'complete', result }\\nconst token = await encode({\\n  token: result,\\n  secret: process.env.AUTH_SECRET!,\\n  salt: SESSION_COOKIE,\\n  maxAge: SESSION_MAX_AGE,\\n})\\nconst cookie = [\\n  `${SESSION_COOKIE}=${token}`,\\n  `Max-Age=${SESSION_MAX_AGE}`,\\n  'Path=/',\\n  'HttpOnly',\\n  'Secure',\\n  'SameSite=None',\\n  'Partitioned',\\n].join('; ')\\nreturn new Response(null, {\\n  status: 204,\\n  headers: { 'set-cookie': cookie, 'cache-control': 'no-store' },\\n})\\n```\\n\\nSet `Secure` unconditionally. Abort `signal` when the component\\n * unmounts; a mounted flag instead stays false under Strict Mode's extra cleanup in development.\\n */\\nexport async function waitForPreviewOAuthSession(\\n  secret: string,\\n  signal: AbortSignal,\\n  win: Window = window,\\n): Promise<'complete' | 'expired' | 'aborted'> {\\n  const deadline = Date.now() + EXCHANGE_TIMEOUT_MS\\n  // Ends a request or delay in flight, whether the caller aborts or the transaction expires.\\n  const stop = new AbortController()\\n  const abort = () => stop.abort()\\n  const expiry = win.setTimeout(abort, EXCHANGE_TIMEOUT_MS)\\n  signal.addEventListener('abort', abort)\\n  if (signal.aborted) abort()\\n  try {\\n    while (!stop.signal.aborted && Date.now() < deadline) {\\n      const response = await win.fetch('/api/auth/preview-exchange', {\\n        method: 'POST',\\n        headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\\n        body: JSON.stringify({ secret }),\\n        signal: stop.signal,\\n      })\\n      if (response.status === 204) return 'complete'\\n      if (response.status === 410) return 'expired'\\n      if (response.status !== 202) throw new Error('Preview sign-in could not be completed')\\n      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {\\n        const done = () => {\\n          win.clearTimeout(timer)\\n          stop.signal.removeEventListener('abort', done)\\n          resolve()\\n        }\\n        const timer = win.setTimeout(done, EXCHANGE_POLL_MS)\\n        stop.signal.addEventListener('abort', done)\\n      })\\n    }\\n  } catch (error) {\\n    if (!stop.signal.aborted) throw error\\n  } finally {\\n    win.clearTimeout(expiry)\\n    signal.removeEventListener('abort', abort)\\n  }\\n  return signal.aborted ? 'aborted' : 'expired'\\n}\\n\\n/** Runs on the fixed same-origin signin bridge, before visiting the provider. */\\nexport async function startPreviewOAuthBridge(\\n  start: (secret: string) => Promise<string>,\\n  win: Window = window,\\n): Promise<void> {\\n  const opener = win.opener as Window | null\\n  if (!opener || win.location.search || win.location.hash) {\\n    throw new Error('Open preview sign-in from the app')\\n  }\\n  const secret = randomSecret(win)\\n  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\\n    const cleanup = () => {\\n      win.clearTimeout(timer)\\n      win.removeEventListener('message', receive)\\n    }\\n    const receive = (event: MessageEvent) => {\\n      if (\\n        event.source !== opener ||\\n        event.origin !== win.location.origin ||\\n        event.data?.type !== ACK ||\\n        event.data.secret !== secret\\n      )\\n        return\\n      cleanup()\\n      resolve()\\n    }\\n    const timer = win.setTimeout(() => {\\n      cleanup()\\n      reject(new Error('Preview OAuth opener did not connect'))\\n    }, HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS)\\n    win.addEventListener('message', receive)\\n    opener.postMessage({ type: READY, secret }, win.location.origin)\\n  })\\n  let authorizationUrl: string\\n  try {\\n    authorizationUrl = await start(secret)\\n  } catch (error) {\\n    opener.postMessage({ type: FAILED, secret }, win.location.origin)\\n    throw error\\n  }\\n  // Prevent iframe polling from racing transaction creation.\\n  opener.postMessage({ type: STARTED, secret }, win.location.origin)\\n  win.location.assign(authorizationUrl)\\n}\\n\\n// Strict Mode runs effects twice in development. {"toolCallId":"57874e33-b2d5-8040-be72-ae006f84f186","toolName":"figaro.plugin/skill","resultJson":"{\"success\":true,\"content\":\"import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'\\n\\nconst SECRET = /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/\\nconst TRANSACTION_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000\\n// Figma's callback host forwards at most this much.\\nconst MAX_CALLBACK_LENGTH = 8192\\n\\nexport const newPreviewOAuthSecret = () => randomBytes(32).toString('hex')\\n\\n/** The origin is the configured browser-facing sandbox origin, never a request header. */\\nexport function isPreviewOAuthPost(request: Request, trustedOrigin: string): boolean {\\n  return (\\n    request.method === 'POST' &&\\n    request.headers.get('origin') === trustedOrigin &&\\n    request.headers.get('content-type')?.split(';')[0].trim() === 'application/json'\\n  )\\n}\\n\\n/** Validate bootstrap CSRF on start in addition to the same-origin POST check. */\\nexport function hasPreviewOAuthCsrf(cookie: string | undefined, submitted: unknown): boolean {\\n  return typeof cookie === 'string' && SECRET.test(cookie) && cookie === submitted\\n}\\n\\n/** Reads the fragment the callback page POSTs; its parameters are the provider's query. */\\nexport function readPreviewOAuthCallback(body: unknown): URLSearchParams | null {\\n  const callback = (body as { callback?: unknown } | null)?.callback\\n  if (typeof callback !== 'string' || !callback || callback.length > MAX_CALLBACK_LENGTH) {\\n    return null\\n  }\\n  return new URLSearchParams(callback)\\n}\\n\\ntype Transaction<T> = {\\n  expires: number\\n  nonce: string\\n  verifier: string\\n  phase: 'pending' | 'exchanging' | 'complete'\\n  result?: T\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * Share one instance across routes and HMR; {"toolCallId":"28b8f1fd-b762-86eb-860b-54beacf85d88","toolName":"figaro.plugin/skill","resultJson":"{\"success\":true,\"content\":\"# Payload Data via CLI\\n\\nRun content commands from the project root. The platform supplies the backend\\nenvironment to agent-launched commands. Never inspect, print, persist, replace,\\nor ask the user for those values. In this experimental configuration, use the\\nCLI even when project-level guidance recommends Payload MCP.\\n\\n## Discover the installed command contract\\n\\nDo not assume operation names, arguments, flags, output shapes, or capabilities.\\nDiscover the interface installed in the current project for every content task:\\n\\n1. Run `figma make verify-bootstrap` and wait for it to succeed. This waits for\\n   bootstrap to complete and the development server to report ready.\\n2. Run `pnpm exec payload --help` directly and capture its complete output and\\n   exit status. This lists the available operations.\\n3. Choose an operation only when the top-level help lists it.\\n4. Run `pnpm exec payload <operation> --help` for each operation you plan to use.\\n5. Use only the arguments and flags documented by those help calls.\\n\\nTreat a missing required content operation, such as `createDocuments`, as an\\noutdated CLI even when `pnpm exec payload --help` succeeds. When `payload` is older than 4.0.0-canary.32, upgrade it\\nand its version-coupled packages to 4.0.0-canary.32 or newer, regenerate the\\nlockfile, wait for the development server to reload, verify bootstrap again,\\nand rediscover help.\\n\\nIf the installed version is already 4.0.0-canary.32 or newer, or help still\\ndoes not expose the required capability after the upgrade, report the missing\\noperation and stop. Do not infer one collection or global's fields from another.\\n\\n## Pass structured input as a file\\n\\n`--input <json|@file|->` takes the complete command input. For a local file, use a path relative to the project\\nroot:\\n\\n```json\\n{ \\\"slug\\\": \\\"media\\\", \\\"documents\\\": [{ \\\"data\\\": { \\\"alt\\\": \\\"Burger\\\" }, \\\"file\\\": \\\"public/burger.jpg\\\" }] }\\n```\\n\\nFor an external image URL, use an `externalURL` object. Prefer CLI uploads over manual uploads\\nor plain URL fields.\\n\\n## Read before writing\\n\\nBefore a mutation:\\n\\n1. If the target collection or global does not exist, create it with\\n   `payload-data-modeling`.\\n2. Inspect its schema and all required fields.\\n3. {"text":"Kelima layar dan alur TrueCost SMAHADA berhasil dibuat serta terintegrasi dengan Next.js + Payload.

### Fitur yang diterapkan

1. **Login dan sistem akun**
   - Login email/password
   - Pendaftaran akun siswa
   - Google Sign-In
   - Profil/inisial pengguna di header
   - Logout terpisah dari akun admin CMS

2. **Live Camera Scanner**
   - Akses kamera perangkat dengan rasio 4:3
   - Viewfinder hijau bercahaya
   - Animasi garis pemindai
   - Tombol shutter **Scan Produk**
   - Fallback ramah pengguna ketika kamera tidak tersedia

3. **Overview Dampak**
   - Produk hasil scan
   - Jejak karbon, berat plastik, dan kandungan gula
   - Callout edukasi **Tahukah Kamu?**
   - CTA merah **❌ Gak Jadi Beli**
   - CTA hijau **✅ Jadi Beli**

4. **Selebrasi “Gak Jadi Beli”**
   - Overlay layar penuh
   - Animasi konfeti
   - Ringkasan emisi yang dicegah
   - Tombol kembali ke Dashboard

5. **Konfirmasi “Jadi Beli”**
   - Konfirmasi pencatatan emisi
   - Data tersimpan ke Habit Tracker
   - Otomatis kembali ke Dashboard

### Backend dan keamanan

- Koleksi Payload `users` untuk akun siswa
- Koleksi `habit-logs` untuk aktivitas milik pengguna
- Data pengguna dipisahkan dari akun admin CMS
- Access rule membatasi log berdasarkan pemilik
- Server menentukan pemilik log secara otomatis
- Google OAuth mendukung published site dan preview Figma melalui PKCE, CSRF, popup bridge, dan session exchange
- Route `/tracker` tetap tersedia

### Verifikasi

- Payload bootstrap berhasil
- Schema `users` dan `habit-logs` berhasil diverifikasi
- TypeScript `tsc --noEmit` berhasil
- Production build berhasil
- `figma make verify-deploy` berhasil
- `/` dan `/tracker` merespons `200`
- Google OAuth menghasilkan redirect `302` valid
- Kasus query preview ilegal ditolak `400`
- Cross-origin preview request ditolak `403`

{"text":"Tolong buatkan dan integrasikan komponen antarmuka web interaktif untuk aplikasi TrueCost SMAHADA yang menghubungkan live camera view dengan logika pemindaian model AI Edge Impulse.

Tolong rancang dalam struktur kode komponen (HTML/JS) atau layout fungsional dengan ketentuan berikut:

1. Area Live Camera & Pemindai:

    Sediakan elemen tag HTML <video id="webcam" autoplay playsinline> dengan gaya kontainer rounded box yang bersih.

    Tampilkan lapisan overlay bingkai pemindai (glowing viewfinder frame) di atas video untuk memberikan visualisasi proses scanning.

2. Inisialisasi & Eksekusi Skrip Edge Impulse (JavaScript):

    Tuliskan fungsi inisialisasi yang memuat pustaka Edge Impulse WASM/Standalone dari folder lokal (model/edge-impulse-standalone.js).

    Buat fungsi asinkron scanJajanan() yang mengambil frame gambar dari elemen video kamera secara real-time dan memasukkannya ke dalam fungsi classifier.classify(videoElement).

3. Penanganan Hasil Prediksi AI (Classification Result):

    Ambil label dengan probabilitas tertinggi (topResult.label dan topResult.value).

    Berikan logika kondisional: jika akurasi value > 0.6, otomatis panggil fungsi pop-up fakta dampak lingkungan (menampilkan estimasi jejak karbon dalam gCO₂e, sampah plastik, dan kandungan gula).

    Jika di bawah 0.6, tampilkan teks indikator status: 'Mengarahkan kamera... Posisikan kemasan Minuman Botol, Saset, atau Ciki di dalam bingkai'.

4. Tombol Keputusan Pengguna (CTA):

    Sertakan dua tombol aksi utama pada pop-up hasil deteksi:

        Tombol Merah: ❌ Gak Jadi Beli (memicu screen selebrasi pengurangan emisi).

        Tombol Hijau: ✅ Jadi Beli (mencatat data ke habit tracker harian)."","providerOptions":{}}

{"text":"Integrasi live camera dengan model **Edge Impulse WASM** dari lampiran telah selesai.

### Implementasi utama

- Model lokal tersedia di:
  - `/model/edge-impulse-standalone.js`
  - `/model/edge-impulse-classifier.js`
  - `/model/edge-impulse-standalone.wasm`
- Kamera menggunakan:
  ```html
  <video id="webcam" autoplay playsinline>
  ```
- Viewfinder hijau dan animasi garis pemindai tetap tersedia.
- Adapter `EdgeImpulseVideoClassifier`:
  - Menangkap frame video menggunakan canvas
  - Menyesuaikan resolusi berdasarkan properti model
  - Mengubah piksel menjadi fitur RGB Edge Impulse
  - Menyediakan API `classifier.classify(videoElement)`

### Logika klasifikasi

Fungsi `scanJajanan()` sekarang:

1. Mengambil frame langsung dari kamera.
2. Menjalankan klasifikasi Edge Impulse.
3. Mengurutkan hasil berdasarkan probabilitas.
4. Mengambil `topResult.label` dan `topResult.value`.
5. Jika confidence lebih dari `0.6`:
   - Menampilkan produk yang terdeteksi
   - Menutup kamera
   - Membuka **Overview Dampak**
6. Jika confidence kurang dari `0.6`, menampilkan:
   - **“Mengarahkan kamera... Posisikan kemasan Minuman Botol, Saset, atau Ciki di dalam bingkai”**

Label hasil AI juga disimpan sebagai nama produk ketika pengguna memilih **Jadi Beli** atau **Gak Jadi Beli**.

### CTA terintegrasi

- **❌ Gak Jadi Beli**
  - Menyimpan aktivitas ke Payload
  - Membuka layar selebrasi pengurangan emisi

- **✅ Jadi Beli**
  - Menyimpan produk terdeteksi ke Habit Tracker
  - Menampilkan konfirmasi
  - Kembali otomatis ke Dashboard

### Verifikasi

- TypeScript berhasil
- Production deployment verification berhasil
- `/`, `/tracker`, dan `/education` merespons `200`
- JavaScript model merespons `200`
- WASM merespons `200` dengan MIME `application/wasm`
- `git diff --check` berhasil

Pengujian inferensi kamera secara langsung tetap memerlukan izin kamera pada perangkat melalui preview HTTPS.","textMode":"visible_message"}

{"text":""Tolong buatkan dan perbaiki kode sumber aplikasi web interaktif TrueCost SMAHADA dengan ketentuan teknis dan fungsional yang sangat spesifik sebagai berikut:

1. Sistem Autentikasi (Login, Register & Logout Berbasis Username Saja):

    Perbaiki bug pada alur login, daftar, dan logout yang sebelumnya rusak.

    Aturan Pendaftaran: Gunakan hanya Username dan Password (tanpa login Google dan tanpa opsi email). Di balik layar, buatkan sistem yang mengonversi username secara otomatis menjadi format email tiruan (contoh: username@truecost.smahada) agar kompatibel dengan Firebase Authentication, serta simpan profil pengguna ke Firestore.

    Pastikan sesi pengguna terkelola dengan baik (onAuthStateChanged), tombol Logout berfungsi menghapus sesi aktif, dan halaman teralihkan dengan mulus.

2. Integrasi Model AI (Disamarkan):

    Integrasikan skrip model Edge Impulse (edge-impulse-standalone.js).

    Aturan Teks Antarmuka: Jangan pernah menyebutkan istilah 'Edge Impulse' di UI atau teks yang dibaca pengguna. Ubah semua label/status keluaran model menjadi "Hasil Analisis AI".

    Penanganan Unknown: Jika model memberikan hasil prediksi berupa unknown atau tingkat akurasi (confidence) di bawah threshold, tampilkan teks pesan persis: "Ada kesalahan, silahkan coba lagi".

    Penyelarasan Label Objek:

        Ubah kategori label chips menjadi "Snack Keripik".

        Ubah kategori label min\_sachet menjadi "Minuman Sachet".

3. Basis Data Jejak Karbon, Gula, & Natrium (Beserta Rujukan Terbuka):

    Perbarui database objek lokal/Firestore dengan data estimasi nutrisi dan emisi terbaru yang akurat:

        Snack Keripik: Emisi sekitar 80–130 gCO₂e, kandungan natrium tinggi, gula rendah. (Rujukan terverifikasi: Agribalyse Food Database / ADEME).

        Minuman Sachet: Emisi sekitar 60–110 gCO₂e, kandungan gula sangat tinggi (bisa mencapai 15–20g per saset). (Rujukan terverifikasi: Open Food Facts Impact Database).

    Pastikan tautan rujukan tersebut dapat diklik dan dibuka oleh pengguna di bagian informasi detail produk.

4. Visualisasi Data: Heatmap & Daily Activity yang Responsif:

    Buat komponen Activity Heatmap (mirip kontribusi commit GitHub atau pelacak habit) dan grafik aktivitas harian (Daily Activity) yang 100% responsif menyesuaikan ukuran layar perangkat (Mobile, Tablet, Desktop).

    Heatmap dan grafik harus merender data jejak karbon harian pengguna dengan gradasi warna yang intuitif.

5. Manajemen Waktu Real-Time & Navigasi Tanggal (History):

    Waktu & Tanggal Saat Ini: Inisialisasi sistem pencatatan transaksi/pemindaian menggunakan tanggal dan waktu aktual perangkat saat ini (WIB/zona waktu lokal).

    Fitur Arsip / Riwayat Lampau: Sediakan kontrol navigasi kalender atau pemilih tanggal (Date Picker / Month Selector) agar pengguna dapat melihat kembali catatan pemindaian, total jejak karbon, serta data heatmap dari bulan-bulan lalu dan tanggal-tanggal lalu yang tersimpan di database."","providerOptions":{}}

{"text":"Perbaikan dan integrasi teknis TrueCost SMAHADA telah selesai.

### Autentikasi username-only

- Login dan pendaftaran kini hanya menampilkan:
  - Username
  - Password
- Tidak ada lagi opsi Google atau input email.
- Username otomatis dikonversi secara internal:
  - `siswa_smahada` → `siswa_smahada@truecost.smahada`
- Menggunakan Firebase Authentication:
  - `createUserWithEmailAndPassword`
  - `signInWithEmailAndPassword`
  - `onAuthStateChanged`
  - `signOut`
- Profil username dan zona waktu disimpan di Firestore.
- Logout menghapus sesi Firebase aktif dan mengembalikan UI ke keadaan login.
- Integrasi Auth.js dan Google sebelumnya telah dihapus sepenuhnya.

### Analisis AI

- Model lokal tetap menggunakan aset WASM yang sudah diunggah.
- Tidak ada penyebutan teknologi model internal pada antarmuka.
- Seluruh hasil ditampilkan sebagai **Hasil Analisis AI**.
- Penyelarasan label:
  - `chips` → **Snack Keripik**
  - `min_sachet` → **Minuman Sachet**
- Prediksi `unknown`, label yang tidak dikenali, atau confidence ≤ 0,6 menampilkan pesan persis:
  - **“Ada kesalahan, silahkan coba lagi”**

### Database dampak produk

**Snack Keripik**
- Emisi: 80–130 gCO₂e
- Natrium tinggi
- Gula rendah
- Rujukan: Agribalyse Food Database / ADEME

**Minuman Sachet**
- Emisi: 60–110 gCO₂e
- Gula hingga 15–20 gram per saset
- Rujukan: Open Food Facts Impact Database

Tautan rujukan tersedia dan dapat dibuka langsung dari modal detail produk.

### Firestore dan riwayat

Setiap aktivitas menyimpan:

- Produk hasil analisis
- Keputusan beli atau batal
- Jejak karbon
- Sampah plastik
- Gula
- Natrium
- Timestamp aktual perangkat
- Zona waktu lokal pengguna

Struktur penyimpanan:

```text
users/{userId}
users/{userId}/habitLogs/{logId}
```

File `firestore.rules` juga telah ditambahkan untuk membatasi profil dan log hanya kepada pemilik akun.

### Visualisasi dan arsip

- Heatmap aktivitas bulanan yang responsif
- Gradasi hijau, kuning, dan merah berdasarkan dampak
- Grafik Daily Activity responsif
- Month selector
- Navigasi bulan sebelumnya dan berikutnya
- Riwayat aktivitas sesuai bulan terpilih
- Waktu ditampilkan menggunakan zona waktu lokal perangkat
- Rekap karbon dihasilkan langsung dari data Firestore realtime

### Verifikasi

- TypeScript berhasil
- Firebase SDK berhasil terpasang
- Payload bootstrap tetap sehat
- `figma make verify-deploy` berhasil
- `/`, `/tracker`, dan `/education` merespons `200`
- Seluruh aset model JavaScript/WASM merespons `200`
- Auth.js dan route Google lama sudah tidak tersedia

### Konfigurasi Firebase yang perlu dipastikan

Di Firebase Console:

1. Aktifkan **Authentication → Sign-in method → Email/Password**.  
   Email hanya dipakai secara internal; pengguna tetap login memakai username.
2. Buat database **Cloud Firestore**.
3. Publikasikan aturan dari `firestore.rules` agar profil dan log pengguna dapat disimpan dengan aman.","textMode":"visible_message"}

- Fix Bug Daftar & Email Mapping: Perbaiki error 'username sudah digunakan/terjadi kesalahan'. - Mode Trial (Device Storage): Sediakan tombol 'Coba Tanpa Akun / Trial'. Jika dipilih, simpan seluruh data riwayat, jejak karbon, dan aktivitas harian secara lokal di perangkat pengguna menggunakan localStorage tanpa perlu terhubung ke Firebase Auth.
- Manajemen Sesi & Logout: Pastikan tombol Logout berfungsi dengan bersih menghapus sesi aktif dan mengembalikan pengguna ke halaman utama/login.

2. Opsi Input Manual & Kategori Jajanan Variatif:
- Sediakan menu/tab Input Manual selain pemindaian kamera. Strukturkan menggunakan array objek terpusat (categories) agar hemat token namun memuat pilihan jajanan kantin yang kaya dan luas:
- Plastik / Kemasan Fleksibel:
    - Snack Keripik / Ciki (\~110 gCO₂e, Natrium Tinggi, Gula Rendah)
    - Minuman Sachet Bubuk / Kopi (\~90 gCO₂e, Gula Tinggi \~15g)
    - Biskuit / Oreo Kemasan Plastik (\~80 gCO₂e, Gula Tinggi, Natrium Sedang)
    - Botol Minum Plastik Kemasan (\~150 gCO₂e)
    - Es Teh Plastik / Jelly Cup (\~40 gCO₂e, Gula Tinggi)
    - Roti Bungkus Plastik (\~70 gCO₂e)
    - Sosis / Nugget Kemasan Plastik (\~130 gCO₂e)
- Kardus / Kertas / Kotak:
    - Kotak Snack / Pocky / Wafer Box (\~60 gCO₂e, Gula Sedang)
    - Kemasan Susu Kotak Tetra (\~80 gCO₂e)
    - Cup Mie Instan / Paper Cup (\~100 gCO₂e)
    - Gorengan Bungkus Kertas Cokelat (\~50 gCO₂e)
- Kaleng / Kaca (Pendukung):
    - Minuman Kaleng Soda / Susu (\~180 gCO₂e)
    - Botol Kaca Sirup / Teh (\~220 gCO₂e)

3. Integrasi Model Analisis AI & Penanganan Error:
- Hubungkan pemindai kamera dengan model deteksi objek.
- Aturan Label UI: Jangan pernah menampilkan istilah 'Edge Impulse' di antarmuka pengguna. Selalu tampilkan sebagai 'Hasil Analisis AI'.

- Penyelarasan Label Objek AI:
- Deteksi chips -> Tampilkan sebagai 'Snack Keripik'.
- Deteksi min\_sachet -> Tampilkan sebagai 'Minuman Sachet'.

4. Activity Heatmap & Kalender Responsif Mobile:
- Rancang komponen Activity Heatmap yang 100% mobile-friendly (menggunakan CSS Grid/flex overflow-x yang halus tanpa memerlukan zoom-out seperti tampilan desktop).
- Data Waktu Akurat: Sinkronkan tanggal, bulan, dan tahun secara real-time merujuk pada waktu lokal perangkat pengguna saat ini.
- Fitur Riwayat (History Navigation): Setiap kotak/sel heatmap harus memuat informasi tanggal yang presisi (saat di-hover/diklik), serta sediakan navigasi pemilih tanggal/bulan agar pengguna dapat melihat catatan aktivitas pada tanggal dan bulan-bulan lalu.

5. Tab Edukasi (Materi Jejak Karbon & Artikel Rujukan):
- Sediakan tab Edukasi interaktif berisi ringkasan penjelasan tentang apa itu carbon footprint serta alur siklus rantai pasok bagaimana jajanan bisa sampai ke tangan konsumen.
- Tampilkan link artikel eksternal yang aktif dan dapat dikunjungi langsung (contoh: BBC Science Focus - Carbon Footprint https://www.sciencefocus.com/).

{"text":"Pemeriksaan duplikasi upgrade tidak menemukan pekerjaan setara (remote bukan GitHub, sehingga pemeriksaan PR memang tidak tersedia). Saya kini menerapkan alur trial/Firebase, katalog manual terpusat, kalender interaktif, materi edukasi, aset model terbaru, serta guard bootstrap agar error `FIGMA_EID` tidak lagi dicetak saat backend belum diprovisikan.Upgrade Next.js 16.4.3 dan aset model baru sudah terpasang. Implementasi utama juga selesai; saya beralih ke verifikasi tipe, build, route publik, dan pemeriksaan khusus bootstrap agar masalah environment benar-benar tidak muncul kembali.TypeScript dan bootstrap live preview kini lulus; script dev juga sudah mengikuti kontrak supervisor (`exec`) dan melewati pembuatan import map secara bersih saat `FIGMA_EID` belum tersedia, tanpa stack trace error. Selanjutnya saya memverifikasi build produksi dan ketiga route publik.Verifikasi produksi menemukan sumber kedua dari error yang sama: skrip publish selalu menjalankan `payload build` meskipun environment Payload belum terhubung. Saya akan membuat fallback resmi ke `next build` hanya ketika `FIGMA_EID` tidak tersedia, sehingga frontend tetap dapat dibangun tanpa memalsukan secret atau mengubah internals Payload.Build produksi berhasil mengompilasi kode, tetapi prerender `/tracker` mengungkap masalah terpisah: Firebase diinisialisasi saat server build walaupun variabel publik hanya tersedia di runtime browser. Saya akan mengubahnya menjadi inisialisasi browser-lazy dengan fallback trial, sehingga halaman dapat diprerender tanpa API key dan autentikasi tetap aktif saat konfigurasi Firebase tersedia.Build produksi kini lulus dan route `/`, `/tracker`, serta `/education` semuanya diprerender statis. Saya melakukan pemeriksaan akhir terhadap respons live, aset WASM, diff keamanan, dan status Git sebelum menutup pekerjaan.## Selesai diperbaiki

### Autentikasi dan trial
- Mapping username kini menggunakan `username@appmail.com`.
- Pendaftaran memeriksa dokumen `usernames/{username}` sebelum membuat Firebase Auth.
- Ditambahkan transaction untuk mencegah duplikasi username secara bersamaan.
- Pesan error pendaftaran dibuat lebih spesifik.
- Mode **Coba Tanpa Akun / Trial** menyimpan seluruh aktivitas di `localStorage`.
- Logout membersihkan sesi aktif tanpa menghapus riwayat trial tersimpan.
- Firebase sekarang diinisialisasi secara lazy di browser, sehingga build tidak gagal ketika konfigurasi Firebase tidak tersedia saat prerender.
- `firestore.rules` ditambahkan aturan namespace username yang hanya mengizinkan pemeriksaan satu username, bukan listing.

### Tracker
- Ditambahkan pilihan **Pindai Kamera** dan **Input Manual**.
- Katalog terpusat berisi 13 kategori jajanan plastik, kertas/kardus, kaleng, dan kaca.
- Setiap produk menampilkan:
  - estimasi karbon;
  - plastik;
  - gula;
  - natrium;
  - catatan nutrisi;
  - tautan aktif Agribalyse atau Open Food Facts.
- Model AI terbaru dari lampiran telah dipasang.
- Label model diselaraskan:
  - `chips` → Snack Keripik;
  - `min_sachet` → Minuman Sachet.
- Confidence di bawah 60%, label tidak dikenal, atau kegagalan analisis menampilkan:
  - **“Ada kesalahan, silahkan coba lagi”**
- Istilah “Edge Impulse” dan emoji aksi tidak tampil di UI.

### Heatmap dan riwayat
- Heatmap kini responsif tanpa layout desktop yang dipaksakan.
- Tanggal menggunakan waktu lokal perangkat.
- Setiap sel menampilkan tanggal dan ringkasan aktivitas melalui label aksesibel.
- Sel dapat diklik untuk membuka riwayat tanggal tersebut.
- Ditambahkan pemilih tanggal, bulan, serta navigasi bulan sebelumnya/berikutnya.
- Grafik aktivitas menyesuaikan lebar layar mobile.

### Edukasi
- Penjelasan carbon footprint diperluas.
- Lima tahap rantai pasok dibuat interaktif.
- Ditambahkan artikel dan basis data aktif:
  - BBC Science Focus;
  - Agribalyse ADEME;
  - Open Food Facts.

### Payload, bootstrap, dan keamanan
- Startup tidak lagi menjalankan `generate:importmap` ketika `FIGMA_EID` belum tersedia.
- Script dev sekarang menggunakan `exec` agar sesuai kontrak supervisor Make.
- Publish memiliki fallback ke build route publik Next.js jika environment Payload belum terhubung.
- Next.js berhasil ditingkatkan dari **16.4.0 ke 16.4.3**.
- `experimental.agentUpgrade` disetel ke `security`.

## Verifikasi

- TypeScript `tsc --noEmit`: lulus.
- Bootstrap live preview: lulus.
- Verifikasi produksi: lulus.
- Route produksi:
  - `/` — statis
  - `/tracker` — statis
  - `/education` — statis
- Pemeriksaan live:
  - `/` — 200
  - `/tracker` — 200
  - `/education` — 200
  - model WASM — 200
  - classifier JS — 200
- `git diff --check`: lulus.
- Cached preview tidak diperiksa.

Catatan: workspace ini masih tidak menyediakan `FIGMA_EID`, sehingga halaman publik memakai fallback yang sudah diverifikasi. Payload Admin/API baru berfungsi penuh ketika environment Payload/Figma diprovisikan oleh platform. Aturan `firestore.rules` juga perlu diterapkan ke proyek Firebase terkait agar namespace username baru aktif.","textMode":"visible_message"}

{"text":"Tolong buatkan, perbaiki, dan sempurnakan seluruh kode sumber aplikasi web TrueCost SMAHADA dengan spesifikasi teknis dan fungsional yang presisi dan hemat token berikut:

1. Autentikasi Firebase & Mode Trial Lokal:
- Fix Bug Daftar & Email Mapping: Perbaiki error 'username sudah digunakan/terjadi kesalahan'. Saat pengguna mendaftar menggunakan Username, buat skema email mapping otomatis menggunakan domain umum yang bersih tanpa unsur kata 'smahada' (contoh: [username]@appmail.com atau [username]@userdomain.net). Lakukan validasi dokumen Firestore terhadap ketersediaan username sebelum memanggil Firebase Auth.
- Mode Trial (Device Storage): Sediakan tombol 'Coba Tanpa Akun / Trial'. Jika dipilih, simpan seluruh data riwayat, jejak karbon, dan aktivitas harian secara lokal di perangkat pengguna menggunakan localStorage tanpa perlu terhubung ke Firebase Auth.
- Manajemen Sesi & Logout: Pastikan tombol Logout berfungsi dengan bersih menghapus sesi aktif dan mengembalikan pengguna ke halaman utama/login.

2. Opsi Input Manual & Kategori Jajanan Variatif:
- Sediakan menu/tab Input Manual selain pemindaian kamera. Strukturkan menggunakan array objek terpusat (categories) agar hemat token namun memuat pilihan jajanan kantin yang kaya dan luas:
- Plastik / Kemasan Fleksibel:
    - Snack Keripik / Ciki (\~110 gCO₂e, Natrium Tinggi, Gula Rendah)
    - Minuman Sachet Bubuk / Kopi (\~90 gCO₂e, Gula Tinggi \~15g)
    - Biskuit / Oreo Kemasan Plastik (\~80 gCO₂e, Gula Tinggi, Natrium Sedang)
    - Botol Minum Plastik Kemasan (\~150 gCO₂e)
    - Es Teh Plastik / Jelly Cup (\~40 gCO₂e, Gula Tinggi)
    - Roti Bungkus Plastik (\~70 gCO₂e)
    - Sosis / Nugget Kemasan Plastik (\~130 gCO₂e)
- Kardus / Kertas / Kotak:
    - Kotak Snack / Pocky / Wafer Box (\~60 gCO₂e, Gula Sedang)
    - Kemasan Susu Kotak Tetra (\~80 gCO₂e)
    - Cup Mie Instan / Paper Cup (\~100 gCO₂e)
    - Gorengan Bungkus Kertas Cokelat (\~50 gCO₂e)
- Kaleng / Kaca (Pendukung):
    - Minuman Kaleng Soda / Susu (\~180 gCO₂e)
    - Botol Kaca Sirup / Teh (\~220 gCO₂e)
- Setiap kali sub-kategori dipilih, tampilkan estimasi Jejak Karbon, Gula/Natrium, serta tautan rujukan aktif yang bisa diklik langsung oleh pengguna (Rujukan: Agribalyse ADEME https://agribalyse.ademe.fr/ untuk makanan/snack dan Open Food Facts https://world.openfoodfacts.org/ untuk minuman/kemasan).

3. Integrasi Model Analisis AI & Penanganan Error:
- Hubungkan pemindai kamera dengan model deteksi objek.
- Aturan Label UI: Jangan pernah menampilkan istilah 'Edge Impulse' di antarmuka pengguna. Selalu tampilkan sebagai 'Hasil Analisis AI'.
- Penanganan Error / Unknown: Jika model mendeteksi objek sebagai unknown atau tingkat akurasi (confidence) di bawah threshold, tampilkan teks pesan persis: 'Ada kesalahan, silahkan coba lagi'.
- Penyelarasan Label Objek AI:
- Deteksi chips -> Tampilkan sebagai 'Snack Keripik'.
- Deteksi min\_sachet -> Tampilkan sebagai 'Minuman Sachet'.

4. Activity Heatmap & Kalender Responsif Mobile:
- Rancang komponen Activity Heatmap yang 100% mobile-friendly (menggunakan CSS Grid/flex overflow-x yang halus tanpa memerlukan zoom-out seperti tampilan desktop).
- Data Waktu Akurat: Sinkronkan tanggal, bulan, dan tahun secara real-time merujuk pada waktu lokal perangkat pengguna saat ini.
- Fitur Riwayat (History Navigation): Setiap kotak/sel heatmap harus memuat informasi tanggal yang presisi (saat di-hover/diklik), serta sediakan navigasi pemilih tanggal/bulan agar pengguna dapat melihat catatan aktivitas pada tanggal dan bulan-bulan lalu.

5. Tab Edukasi (Materi Jejak Karbon & Artikel Rujukan):
- Sediakan tab Edukasi interaktif berisi ringkasan penjelasan tentang apa itu carbon footprint serta alur siklus rantai pasok bagaimana jajanan bisa sampai ke tangan konsumen.
- Tampilkan link artikel eksternal yang aktif dan dapat dikunjungi langsung (contoh: BBC Science Focus - Carbon Footprint https://www.sciencefocus.com/).

Run \`next upgrade --agent=security\` and follow its instructions.

{"text":"**Evaluating product labeling**

I’m noticing that the model doesn’t have "kotak_snack" as required. I think we need a map for future models, but it’s currently unknown. Maybe I can add a category ID "snack_box" and possibly alias "kotak_snack" to "snack_box." The required label should be "Kotak Snack / Kardus," but right now it’s labeled "Kotak Snack / Pocky / Wafer Box." I’m considering if we should manually adjust this or even add an AI label separately to clarify the product details.

**Considering category adjustments and layout**

I’m seeing that adding a manual category duplicate would create extra complications, so maybe using a filter could help. The model needs to label the category as "Kotak Snack / Kardus," and I think adding details as a subtitle might work. 

For the mobile interface, I want to implement a bottom navigation with Home, Tracker, and Education. The current fixed layout has a single FAB, which should be updated for better functionality. Also, I need to ensure action buttons and touch targets comply with size requirements, like minimum dimensions for usability.

**Adjusting grid settings**

I’m thinking it’s better to set a minimum width of 392px for each item with 48px dimensions and 6px gaps, which might bring the total to around 440px. I could use an inner grid with `min-w-[392px]` and enable horizontal scrolling with `overflow-x auto` for a smoother interface. This change should meet the 48px size requirement, and the user has allowed for horizontal scrolling, so it sounds like a solid plan!

**Improving session management**

I’m thinking about adding a TRIAL_SESSION_KEY and using startTrial to set localStorage. After the auth callback, I want to check the trial session and load local logs if there’s no user. I’m also considering creating a helper function called loadTrial. Can I define it inside? When logging out, I'll need to remove the trial session while preserving the logs. Overall, this should make session management more efficient.

**Inspecting registration process**

I'm starting a trial with Firebase, ensuring no users are already in place before the callback is done. It seems there might be a registration bug that I need to catch within a try-finally structure. Alright, I need to work on email mapping and implementing the model label. There's also the need to add a bottom navigation component and include pages, while inspecting the Home structure and tracker icons. I'll make those adjustments first.

{"text":"Implementasi TrueCost SMAHADA telah disempurnakan dengan fokus mobile-first.

### Peningkatan utama

- Trial session kini tetap aktif setelah reload menggunakan `localStorage`.
- Logout membersihkan sesi aktif dan mengarahkan pengguna kembali ke beranda.
- Mapping Firebase tetap memakai `username@appmail.com` dengan validasi username Firestore sebelum Firebase Auth.
- Bottom navigation thumb-friendly ditambahkan pada halaman Beranda, Tracker, dan Edukasi.
- Tombol utama, navigasi, form, kontrol bulan, tanggal, dan modal memakai target sentuh minimal 48px.
- Heatmap menggunakan sel 48px dan horizontal scroll terkontrol untuk layar ponsel sempit.
- Kamera menggunakan konfigurasi portrait 720×1280 dan preview rasio 3:4.
- Frame kamera di-center-crop sesuai rasio input model sehingga tidak terdistorsi.
- Inferensi diberi jeda event-loop sebelum klasifikasi untuk mengurangi UI freezing.
- Label model telah dipetakan:
  - `chips` → **Snack Keripik**
  - `min_sachet` → **Minuman Sachet**
  - `kotak_snack` → **Kotak Snack / Kardus**
- Label unknown atau confidence di bawah 60% tetap menghasilkan pesan persis:
  - **“Ada kesalahan, silahkan coba lagi”**
- UI telah diperiksa dan tidak menampilkan istilah teknis model.
- Aset WASM dan runtime JavaScript dipastikan identik dengan lampiran terbaru.

### Catatan model

Model pada lampiran hanya mengandung kelas `chips`, `min_sachet`, dan `unknown`. Adapter aplikasi sudah mendukung `kotak_snack`, tetapi kelas tersebut baru bisa terdeteksi jika model berikutnya benar-benar mengekspor label itu.

### Verifikasi

- Next.js: **16.4.3**
- `next upgrade --agent=security`: tidak ada security update tambahan.
- TypeScript: lulus.
- Bootstrap Make: lulus.
- Build/deploy verification: lulus.
- Route produksi `/`, `/tracker`, dan `/education`: statis.
- Pemeriksaan live:
  - `/` — 200
  - `/tracker` — 200
  - `/education` — 200
  - WASM model — 200
  - classifier JavaScript — 200
- `git diff --check`: lulus.

{"text":"Tolong buatkan implementasi modul Firebase Autentikasi dan Firestore untuk aplikasi web TrueCost SMAHADA yang dirancang secara super detail, modular, dan "airtight" (tahan banting terhadap error runtime, edge-cases jaringan, serta inkonsistensi data) dengan spesifikasi teknis presisi berikut:

1. Inisialisasi & Modular SDK Setup:
- Gunakan modular Firebase SDK (v10+) dengan inisialisasi aman yang mendukung environment web modern (menggunakan lazy loading atau pengecekan instance agar tidak terjadi error duplicate app initialization).
- Pisahkan konfigurasi kredensial, instance Auth, dan instance Firestore ke dalam modul tersendiri (misalnya \`firebaseConfig.js\`) yang siap diimpor ke modul lain.

2. Skema Email Mapping & Sanitasi Username yang Aman:
- Buat fungsi utilitas pembersih username (\`sanitizeUsername(username)\`): mengubah string menjadi huruf kecil, menghapus spasi di awal/akhir, serta membuang seluruh karakter khusus selain alur alfanumerik dan garis bawah (\`/^[a-z0-9\_]+$/\`).
- Implementasikan fungsi pembuat \*pseudo-email\* (\`generatePseudoEmail(cleanUsername)\`): mengubah username yang sudah dibersihkan menjadi format email umum tanpa menyertakan domain atau unsur kata 'smahada' (contoh: \`[username]@appmail.com\` atau \`[username]@userdomain.net\`).

3. Validasi Firestore Sebelum Pendaftaran (Pre-Registration Check):
- Dalam fungsi \`registerUser(username, password)\`:
- Lakukan validasi ketat: pastikan panjang username minimal 3 karakter dan password minimal 6 karakter. Jika kosong atau tidak valid, throw error deskriptif.
- Lakukan pemeriksaan keberadaan dokumen di koleksi Firestore \`users/{cleanUsername}\` \*sebelum\* memanggil metode Firebase Auth (\`createUserWithEmailAndPassword\`). Jika dokumen dengan ID username tersebut sudah ada, batalkan proses dan kembalikan pesan: \`"Username sudah digunakan, silakan pilih yang lain."\`
- Jika belum ada, buat akun di Firebase Auth menggunakan \*pseudo-email\*, lalu segera buat dokumen baru di Firestore pada path \`users/{cleanUsername}\` yang berisi field: \`uid\` (dari user auth), \`username\` (original/clean), \`email\` (pseudo-email), dan \`createdAt\` (ISO timestamp).
- Bungkus seluruh rangkaian proses pendaftaran dalam blok \`try...catch\` yang komprehensif untuk menangani error spesifik Firebase (seperti \`auth/email-already-in-use\`, \`auth/weak-password\`, atau gangguan jaringan).

4. Alur Login & Penanganan Sesi (Session Handling):
- Dalam fungsi \`loginUser(username, password)\`:
- Sanitasi input username, ubah ke \*pseudo-email\*, lalu panggil \`signInWithEmailAndPassword\`.
- Jika berhasil, hapus flag \`isTrialMode\` dari \`localStorage\` untuk memastikan status sesi akun asli yang aktif.
- Tangani error login gagal dengan pesan yang ramah pengguna (misalnya: \`"Username atau password salah. Silakan coba lagi."\` tanpa membocorkan detail teknis sistem).

5. Manajemen Logout & Pembersihan State:
- Dalam fungsi \`logoutUser()\`:
- Panggil \`signOut(auth)\`.
- Hapus seluruh sisa data sesi lokal yang relevan dari \`localStorage\` (seperti token sementara atau status trial).
- Lakukan pengalihan halaman (\*redirect\*) atau muat ulang halaman secara bersih untuk memastikan memori aplikasi ter-reset total.

6. Mode Trial Lokal (Device Storage Fallback):
- Sediakan fungsi \`activateTrialMode()\` yang menetapkan \`localStorage.setItem("isTrialMode", "true")\`.
- Sediakan fungsi pemantau sesi (\`checkAuthSession(onLoggedIn, onTrial, onLoggedOut)\`):
- Prioritaskan pengecekan \`localStorage\` untuk \`isTrialMode\`. Jika bernilai \`true\`, langsung eksekusi callback \`onTrial()\` tanpa memicu layanan Firebase Auth.
- Jika tidak dalam mode trial, gunakan \`onAuthStateChanged(auth, callback)\` untuk mendeteksi status login secara reaktif, meneruskan objek user ke \`onLoggedIn(user)\` atau memicu \`onLoggedOut()\` jika sesi kosong.","providerOptions":{}}

{"text":"Implementasi Firebase Auth dan Firestore telah dimodularisasi sekaligus memperbaiki hydration mismatch.

### Perbaikan hydration

- State tanggal awal sekarang deterministik:
  - `now` dimulai sebagai `null`.
  - bulan awal `2000-01`.
  - tanggal awal `2000-01-01`.
- Waktu lokal perangkat baru diterapkan dalam `useEffect` setelah hydration.
- Nilai `max` dan status navigasi bulan memakai state waktu lokal, bukan `new Date()` saat SSR.
- HTML server telah diverifikasi menampilkan placeholder deterministik `MEMUAT TANGGAL LOKAL...`.
- Perbedaan tanggal server dan browser tidak lagi memengaruhi hydration.

### Arsitektur Firebase baru

- `src/lib/firebase-config.ts`
  - Menyimpan konfigurasi environment Firebase.
  - Memvalidasi kelengkapan konfigurasi.

- `src/lib/firebase-client.ts`
  - Lazy initialization.
  - Aman terhadap duplicate Firebase app initialization.
  - Tidak menginisialisasi Firebase saat SSR.

- `src/lib/firebase-auth.ts`
  - `sanitizeUsername()`
  - `generatePseudoEmail()`
  - `registerUser()`
  - `loginUser()`
  - `logoutUser()`
  - `activateTrialMode()`
  - `checkAuthSession()`

### Autentikasi

- Username dibersihkan menjadi huruf kecil dengan karakter yang diizinkan hanya `a-z`, `0-9`, dan `_`.
- Pseudo-email menggunakan format `username@appmail.com`.
- Pendaftaran memeriksa `users/{cleanUsername}` sebelum Firebase Auth.
- Dokumen pengguna berisi:
  - `uid`
  - `username`
  - `email`
  - `createdAt` dalam ISO timestamp.
- Jika pembuatan dokumen gagal setelah akun Auth dibuat, akun Auth dihapus kembali untuk mencegah akun yatim.
- Error email terpakai, password lemah, jaringan, permission, timeout, dan terlalu banyak percobaan diterjemahkan menjadi pesan ramah pengguna.
- Login gagal tidak membocorkan detail teknis.

### Session dan trial

- Trial menggunakan key `isTrialMode`.
- `checkAuthSession()` memeriksa trial terlebih dahulu sehingga Firebase Auth tidak diinisialisasi dalam mode trial.
- Login akun menghapus flag trial.
- Logout:
  - menjalankan Firebase `signOut`;
  - membersihkan flag trial dan token sementara;

{"text":"Konfigurasi Firebase asli telah disimpan melalui environment resmi dan digunakan langsung oleh objek `firebaseConfig` tanpa hardcoded secret atau placeholder.

### Konfigurasi

`firebaseConfig` sekarang membaca keenam nilai:

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID`

Seluruh nilai wajib tersedia sebelum Firebase diinisialisasi.

### Inisialisasi modular

Pola inisialisasi telah disesuaikan tepat menjadi:

```ts
const app = getApps().length === 0
  ? initializeApp(firebaseConfig)
  : getApp()
```

Firebase Auth dan Firestore tetap dibuat secara lazy di browser sehingga:

- aman dari duplicate app initialization;
- tidak dieksekusi saat SSR;
- tidak menimbulkan `auth/invalid-api-key` ketika halaman diprerender;
- Mode Demo tidak menginisialisasi Firebase Auth.

### Auth dan Mode Demo

- Register memeriksa `users/{username}` sebelum membuat akun Auth.
- Pseudo-email tetap menggunakan `username@appmail.com`.
- Login menghapus `isTrialMode`.
- Logout menjalankan `signOut`, membersihkan state sesi, lalu hard redirect ke `/`.
- Tombol UI sekarang bertuliskan **Coba Tanpa Akun / Demo**.
- Mode Demo tetap menyimpan aktivitas dan riwayat di `localStorage`.
- Session checker memprioritaskan Mode Demo sebelum Firebase.

### Verifikasi

- Firebase modular SDK: **13.1.0**
- TypeScript: lulus.
- Bootstrap Make: lulus.
- Build produksi: lulus.
- `/`, `/tracker`, `/education`: HTTP 200.
- Tidak ditemukan `auth/invalid-api-key` pada log dev yang tersedia.
- `git diff --check`: lulus.

Nilai kredensial tidak dicetak atau ditulis literal ke repository; nilainya diinjeksikan ke `firebaseConfig` melalui environment agar tetap aman dan dapat digunakan saat preview maupun publish.","textMode":"visible_message"}
